title: The Speed of Sound
description: Thunder booms seconds after lightning flashes. Learn why — and use the speed of sound to reach bell fragment 2.

content.value: Sound Travels Fast — But Light Is Faster

Sound travels quickly through air — about 340 metres every second. That's fast, but LIGHT is far faster. This is why, in a storm, you SEE the lightning first and HEAR the thunder a few seconds later, even though they happen at the same moment.

⚡ Lightning flash  → reaches you almost instantly (light is super fast)
🔊 Thunder boom     → arrives seconds later (sound ~340 m/s)

Count the seconds between them to estimate how far the storm is!

Sound travels at different speeds in different mediums. It moves FASTEST in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases like air. That's because the particles in a solid are packed tightly and pass the vibration along quickly.

SPEED OF SOUND (roughly):
🧱  Solids  → fastest   (particles packed tight)
💧  Liquids → medium
🌬️  Gases   → slowest   (particles far apart)

When sound hits a big hard surface like a cliff or wall, it bounces back. A reflected sound you hear again is an ECHO. Bats and ships use reflected sound to sense objects around them — you'll meet that idea again with ultrasound!
Because sound needs particles to pass the vibration along, denser packing (solids) carries it fastest. No particles at all (vacuum) means no sound.

Key Takeaway: Sound travels about 340 m/s in air — fast, but much slower than light (so thunder lags lightning). It moves fastest in solids and slowest in gases, and it reflects off surfaces to make echoes.

quiz.question: In a storm you see lightning before hearing thunder because…
options: light travels much faster than sound
quiz.explain: Light reaches you almost instantly, while sound travels far slower (~340 m/s), arriving seconds later.

quiz.question: Sound travels FASTEST through…
quiz.explain: Tightly-packed particles in solids pass vibrations along fastest, so sound is fastest in solids.

quiz.question: A sound that reflects off a surface and is heard again is called…
quiz.explain: A reflected sound heard again is an echo.
